frames.b: Ask: do you know one person

reel1.caption:
Your first ten customers are probably already in your phone.

Pick 20 to 30 people who could buy or refer you, send each a personal message with your offer and a photo of your work, and ask if they know one person who needs it. Follow up once, politely.

Send this to a friend who is starting out.

frames.b: For the day a bad review

reel2.caption:
A bad review stings. How you reply matters more than the review.

Stay calm, apologise for their experience, keep the facts short and offer to put it right offline. Future customers are reading your reply, not just the complaint.

Save this for the day a bad review lands.

slides.sub: Your Google Business Profile in 6 steps. Swipe.

slides.title: Get ready
slides.head: Have your real details at hand.
slides.body: Exact business name, address or service area, a phone number you answer, opening hours and at least 5 clear photos.

slides.title: Claim it
slides.head: Search your name on Google Maps first.
slides.body: Someone may have listed you already. Claim it, or add your business, then complete the verification Google asks for.

slides.title: Pick your category
slides.head: Choose the one that matches your main service.
slides.body: Add extras only for services you really offer. Use your real name, not extra keywords.

slides.title: Fill every section
slides.head: Hours, services, description, service area.
slides.body: Two or three plain sentences about what you do and where. Add a WhatsApp or booking link.

slides.title: Add real photos
slides.head: Your work, your van, your team.
slides.body: Natural light, no stock photos, and add new ones at least once a month.

slides.title: Keep it alive
slides.head: Ask happy customers for reviews and reply to all.
slides.body: Never buy or write your own reviews. Update hours the same day anything changes.

slides.sub: Save this for your afternoon off.
